name: Paint
brief: An abstract class for managing graphical elements.
description: A graphical element in TVG is any object composed into a Canvas. Paint represents such a graphical object and its behaviors such as duplication, transformation and composition. TVG recommends the user to regard a paint as a set of volatile commands. They can prepare a Paint and then request a Canvas to run them.

members.name: parent
members.brief: Retrieves the parent paint object.
description: This function returns a pointer to the parent object if the current paint belongs to one. Otherwise, it returns `nullptr`.
members.returns: A pointer to the parent object if available, otherwise `nullptr`.

members.name: visible
members.brief: Sets the visibility of the Paint object.
description: This is useful for selectively excluding paint objects during rendering.

params.name: on
params.description: A boolean flag indicating visibility. The initial value is `true`. `true`, the object will be rendered by the engine. `false`, the object will be excluded from the drawing process.

notes: An invisible object is not considered inactive—it may still participate in internal update processing if its properties are updated, but it will not be taken into account for the final drawing output. To completely deactivate a paint object, remove it from the canvas.

members.name: rotate
members.brief: Sets the angle by which the object is rotated.
description: The angle in measured clockwise from the horizontal axis. The rotational axis passes through the point on the object with zero coordinates.

params.name: degree
params.description: The value of the angle in degrees.

retvals.description: in case a custom transform is applied.

members.name: scale
members.brief: Sets the scale value of the object.

params.name: factor
params.description: The value of the scaling factor. The initial value is 1.

retvals.description: in case a custom transform is applied.

members.name: translate
members.signature: Result translate(float x, float y) noexcept
members.brief: Sets the values by which the object is moved in a two-dimensional space.
description: The origin of the coordinate system is in the upper-left corner of the canvas. The horizontal and vertical axes point to the right and down, respectively.

params.name: x
params.description: The value of the horizontal shift.

params.name: y
params.description: The value of the vertical shift.

retvals.description: in case a custom transform is applied.

members.name: transform
members.brief: Sets the matrix of the affine transformation for the object.
description: The augmented matrix of the transformation is expected to be given.

params.name: m
params.description: The 3x3 augmented matrix.

members.name: transform
members.brief: Gets the matrix of the affine transformation of the object.
description: The values of the matrix can be set by the transform() API, as well by the translate(), scale() and rotate(). In case no transformation was applied, the identity matrix is returned.

members.name: opacity
members.brief: Sets the opacity of the object.

params.name: o
params.description: The opacity value in the range [0 ~ 255], where 0 is completely transparent and 255 is opaque.

notes: Setting the opacity with this API may require multiple render pass for composition. It is recommended to avoid changing the opacity if possible.

members.name: mask
members.signature: Result mask(Paint* target, MaskMethod method) noexcept
members.brief: Sets the masking target object and the masking method.

params.name: target
params.description: The paint of the target object.

params.name: method
params.description: The method used to mask the source object with the target.

retvals.description: if the target has already belonged to another paint.

members.name: clip
members.brief: Clip the drawing region of the paint object.
description: This function restricts the drawing area of the paint object to the specified shape's paths.

params.name: clipper
params.description: The shape object as the clipper.

retvals.description: if the `clipper` has already belonged to another paint.

members.name: blend
members.brief: Sets the blending method for the paint object.
description: The blending feature allows you to combine colors to create visually appealing effects, including transparency, lighting, shading, and color mixing, among others. its process involves the combination of colors or images from the source paint object with the destination (the lower layer image) using blending operations. The blending operation is determined by the chosen `BlendMethod`, which specifies how the colors or images are combined.

params.name: method
params.description: The blending method to be set.

members.name: bounds
members.brief: Retrieves the object-oriented bounding box (OBB) of the paint object in canvas space.
description: This function returns the bounding box of the paint, as an oriented bounding box (OBB) after transformations are applied. The returned values `pt4` may have invalid if the operation fails. Thus, please check the retval.

This bounding box can be used to obtain the transformed bounding region in canvas space by taking the geometry's axis-aligned bounding box (AABB) in the object's local coordinate space and applying the object's transformations.

params.name: pt4
params.description: An array of four points representing the bounding box. The array size must be 4.

retvals.description: If the paint has not been updated by the canvas.

members.name: bounds
members.signature: Result bounds(float* x, float* y, float* w, float* h) noexcept
members.brief: Retrieves the axis-aligned bounding box (AABB) of the paint object in canvas space.
description: Returns the bounding box of the paint as an axis-aligned bounding box (AABB), with all relevant transformations applied. The returned values `x`, `y`, `w`, `h`, may have invalid if the operation fails. Thus, please check the retval.
This bounding box can be used to determine the actual rendered area of the object on the canvas, for purposes such as hit-testing, culling, or layout calculations.

params.name: x
params.description: The x-coordinate of the upper-left corner of the bounding box.

params.name: y
params.description: The y-coordinate of the upper-left corner of the bounding box.

params.name: w
params.description: The width of the bounding box.

params.name: h
params.description: The height of the bounding box.

retvals.description: If the paint has not been updated by the canvas.

members.name: intersects
members.signature: bool intersects(int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t w = 1, int32_t h = 1) noexcept
members.brief: Checks whether a given region intersects the filled area of the paint.
description: This function determines whether the specified rectangular region—defined by (`x`, `y`, `w`, `h`)— intersects the geometric fill region of the paint object.
This is useful for hit-testing purposes, such as detecting whether a user interaction (e.g., touch or click) occurs within a painted region.
The paint must be updated in a Canvas beforehand—typically after the Canvas has been drawn and synchronized.

params.name: x
params.description: The x-coordinate of the top-left corner of the test region.

params.name: y
params.description: The y-coordinate of the top-left corner of the test region.

params.name: w
params.description: The width of the region to test. Must be greater than 0; defaults to 1.

params.name: h
params.description: The height of the region to test. Must be greater than 0; defaults to 1.

members.returns: `true` if any part of the region intersects the filled area; otherwise, `false`.
notes: To test a single point, set the region size to w = 1, h = 1.
For efficiency, an AABB (axis-aligned bounding box) test is performed internally before precise hit detection.
This test does not take into account the results of blending or masking.
This test does take into account hidden paints as well.

members.name: intersects
members.signature: bool intersects(int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t w, int32_t h, bool visibleOnly) noexcept
members.brief: Checks whether a given region intersects the filled area of the paint.
description: This function determines whether the specified rectangular region—defined by (`x`, `y`, `w`, `h`)— intersects the geometric fill region of the paint object.
This is useful for hit-testing purposes, such as detecting whether a user interaction (e.g., touch or click) occurs within a painted region.
The paint must be updated in a Canvas beforehand—typically after the Canvas has been drawn and synchronized.

params.name: x
params.description: The x-coordinate of the top-left corner of the test region.

params.name: y
params.description: The y-coordinate of the top-left corner of the test region.

params.name: w
params.description: The width of the region to test. Must be greater than 0.

params.name: h
params.description: The height of the region to test. Must be greater than 0.

params.name: visibleOnly
params.description: If `true`, hidden paints are excluded from the intersection test.

members.returns: `true` if any part of the region intersects the filled area; otherwise, `false`.
notes: To test a single point, set the region size to w = 1, h = 1.
This test does not take into account the results of blending or masking.

members.name: duplicate
members.brief: Duplicates the object.
description: Creates a new object and sets its all properties as in the original object.
members.returns: The created object when succeed, `nullptr` otherwise.

members.name: opacity
members.brief: Gets the opacity value of the object.
members.returns: The opacity value in the range [0 ~ 255], where 0 is completely transparent and 255 is opaque.

members.name: mask
members.signature: MaskMethod mask(const Paint** target) const noexcept
members.brief: Gets the masking target object and the masking method.

params.name: target
params.description: The paint of the target object.

members.returns: The method used to mask the source object with the target.

members.name: clip
members.brief: Get the clipper shape of the paint object.
description: This function returns the clipper that has been previously set to this paint object.
members.returns: The shape object used as the clipper, or `nullptr` if no clipper is set.

members.name: visible
members.brief: Gets the current visibility status of the Paint object.
members.returns: true if the object is visible and will be rendered. false if the object is hidden and will not be rendered.

members.name: ref
members.brief: Increment the reference count for the Paint instance.
description: This method increases the reference count of the Paint object, allowing shared ownership and control over its lifetime.
members.returns: The updated reference count after the increment by 1.
warnings: Please ensure that each call to ref() is paired with a corresponding call to unref() to prevent a dangling instance.

members.name: unref
members.brief: Decrement the reference count for the Paint instance.
description: This method decreases the reference count of the Paint object by 1. If the reference count reaches zero and the `free` flag is set to true, the Paint instance is automatically deleted.

params.name: free
params.description: Flag indicating whether to delete the Paint instance when the reference count reaches zero.

members.returns: The updated reference count after the decrement.

members.name: refCnt
members.brief: Retrieve the current reference count of the Paint instance.
description: This method provides the current reference count, allowing the user to check the shared ownership state of the Paint object.
members.returns: The current reference count of the Paint instance.

members.name: type
members.brief: Returns the ID value of this class.
description: This method can be used to check the current concrete instance type.
members.returns: The class type ID of the Paint instance.

members.name: id
members.brief: Unique ID of this instance.
description: This is reserved to specify an paint instance in a scene.

members.name: data
members.brief: User-defined data associated with this instance.
description: ThorVG does not interpret or manage the lifetime of this data.

members.name: rel
members.brief: Safely releases a Paint object.
description: This is the counterpart to the `gen()` API, and releases the given Paint object safely, handling `nullptr` and managing ownership properly.

params.name: paint
params.description: A Paint object to release.
